evidence_class: Signed fixture launch grants from LaunchAuthority, fakeredis, the fixture server clock and a fixture network that drops requests, loses responses and repeats a poll response; no live rollout. Live G3 qualification is separate.
interfaces: CommandQueue.issue(execution_id, generation, kind, payload, key, expires_in_ms): the controller issues drain, cancel, answer or stop to the current occupant of a seat; the command id is derived from the swarm, execution and key and never changes, the payload digest covers kind and payload, the same key with the same payload returns the stored command and another payload is revision_conflict; a superseded execution is stale_generation
CommandQueue.outcome(execution_id, command_id): issued, accepted, completed or expired, with accepted_at_ms, completed_at_ms and the reported outcome as separate stored fields

GET /v2/executions/<id>/commands: the credential's own commands that are issued and unexpired or accepted and not yet completed, oldest first, at most poll_limit; an accepted command stays deliverable after its expiry so a worker can still report it; a poll sooner than poll_interval_ms, or one that loses a concurrent stamp, is rate_limited with retry same_request
POST /v2/executions/<id>/commands/<command>/ack: receipt with the payload digest; idempotent, an expired command is refused with expired and never accepted

POST /v2/executions/<id>/commands/<command>/complete: the outcome after acceptance, checkpointed with a checkpoint reference or failed for drain, succeeded, failed or not_run otherwise; idempotent for the same outcome, another outcome is revision_conflict; an unacknowledged command past expiry is expired
scripts.swarm_v2.api.server.Routes(executions, tasks, commands): command paths go to the command endpoints when they are configured

WorkerControl(transport, state_path, handlers): polls, deduplicates by command id, checks the payload digest, stops mutations on a drain before its acknowledgement is confirmed and keeps them stopped unless the server voids an unacknowledged drain by expiry before any checkpoint, refuses answers while draining (not_run) but still runs cancel and stop, runs commands only after the server accepted them, reports a handler error as failed, reports drain checkpoint completion separately and keeps unsent acknowledgements and completions in an fsynced state file
RouteTransport(execution_id, send): the worker side of the endpoints; same_request refusals become ConnectionError for a later retry, other refusals CommandRefused
worker_command_ack_lag_seconds(store, slug): acceptance minus issue time per accepted command

supported_versions.python: 3.11 and 3.12 unit shards in the linked CI run
supported_versions.protocol: SV2-LDG-02 launch grants and registrations; the credential's execution and generation scope every command endpoint
supported_versions.compatibility: The terminal command path in scripts.swarm_v2.runtime.commands and the local swarm are unchanged; the worker command endpoints are additive and Routes without a command API answers command paths as before

states.observed: A command returned by a worker poll; polling changes no command state
states.accepted: The worker acknowledged the payload digest before expiry; accepted_at_ms is stored
states.committed: The worker reported an outcome after acceptance; completed_at_ms and the outcome are stored
states.externally_verified: None; no production deployment and no live rollout yet

authoritative_objects: The worker-commands hash per execution in Redis is authoritative for command state and is never deleted as a cache
The worker state file is authoritative for what the worker already ran; it is written whole through a staged file and replaced
The worker-command-polls hash only rate limits polls and the worker-command-ack-lag list is a measurement, not state
The ledger document is untouched; it stays authoritative for operator work state

rollback_rehearsal.action: Construct CommandQueue with kinds limited to those still allowed: new commands of a removed kind are refused with forbidden_scope while existing commands are still delivered, acknowledged and completed until they finish or expire
rollback_rehearsal.data_safety: No command record is deleted; reissuing an existing key returns the stored command

remaining_limitations: No production process starts the v2 HTTP server or a worker control loop yet; the kind switch is a constructor argument until a deployment package adds an operator control
Command records for an execution are kept after it ends; retention is not yet bounded
A worker whose state file is lost reports an already accepted command as not_run rather than rerunning it; a drain stays in force
A poll refused for a superseded execution raises CommandRefused to the worker loop's caller; acting on it belongs to the worker entrypoint package
may_mutate is a predicate for the agent runtime; wiring it into the agent's tool calls belongs to the worker entrypoint package
The state file is fsynced before its rename, but the folder is not fsynced after it
worker_command_ack_lag_seconds keeps the newest 1000 samples per swarm, without per kind labels

decisions: A worker enters no new mutations mode when it receives a drain, before the server confirmed the acknowledgement: stopping early is safe and a dropped acknowledgement must not let mutations continue

Every command is acknowledged before the worker acts on it, so an expired command is never acted on and a retried acknowledgement returns the stored acceptance without a second run; cancel and stop then run, and an answer runs unless a drain holds, in which case it is reported not_run
Expiry is derived on read from the stored issue time; an unacknowledged command past its expiry is never delivered or accepted, while an accepted command may still report its outcome after expiry
An answer delivered while a drain holds is acknowledged and reported not_run instead of run, because new instructions would start new work; cancel and stop still run because they only end work
A drain stops holding only when the server refused its acknowledgement as expired and no checkpoint was taken; a refusal for a superseded execution or a refused completion keeps the hold

input_preparation.met_by: tests/sv2_ldg05_cases.py builds the fixture from delayed delivery (30 ms of a 50 ms expiry), a duplicated poll response replayed by the fixture network, and a drain whose acknowledgement the network drops

output_contract.met_by: WorkerControl stops mutations on receiving a drain and reports its checkpoint as a separate completion after acceptance

rejection_contract.met_by: An expired command is never delivered or accepted, and a superseded execution cannot poll or be issued commands, so an expired answer or stop never reaches a new conversation

recovery_contract.met_by: Acknowledgement and completion are idempotent per command id; the worker state file records what ran, so a lost response returns the stored outcome without a rerun

mutation_scope.met_by: Command state lives only in the worker-commands Redis hash per execution; no ledger document is opened or written

compatibility.met_by: With the command API configured, the preceding execution endpoints answer byte for byte as before; without it, command paths answer the preceding 404. The local terminal command path in scripts.swarm_v2.runtime.commands is untouched

authority.met_by: Every worker endpoint derives the execution and generation from the signed launch grant bound to its registration (LaunchAuthority.bound), never from the path, body or a display label; a path naming another execution is forbidden_scope. Issuing is the controller's in-process call and is fenced to the current occupant of the seat

state.met_by: The states block of this record separates observed, accepted, committed and externally verified; the store keeps accepted_at_ms and completed_at_ms as separate fields

data_safety.met_by: The authoritative_objects block names the worker-commands hash and the worker state file as authoritative; rollback deletes nothing and reissuing a key returns the stored command

completion_evidence.met_by: interfaces, supported_versions, validation (test outputs), remaining_limitations and rollback_rehearsal blocks of this record
